event_description: Make a splash at Bark in the Waterpark 🐾 Bark in the Waterpark is back at Montage Mountain Resorts on Sunday, September 13th! Bring your pups for a play date, and treat yourself to delicious Lucky One Lemonade or Sweet Tea while you're there. Pups take to the pools from 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM to enjoy doggy paddling, lazy river running, and fun with hundreds of other canines. Montage Mountain Resorts will have doggy vendors on site and plenty of space for your pets to play. Doggy tickets are free, while humans can join in the fun for just $15. Disclaimer For the safety of all in attendance, dogs must be leashed at all times. If your dog becomes aggressive or an issue occurs, you may be asked to leave the premises. Participants are expected to practice responsible pet ownership throughout the day. Dogs must be over four months old, spayed or neutered, and current on all required vaccinations administered by a licensed veterinarian. This includes rabies, DHLPP (Distemper, Hepatitis, Leptospirosis, Parvovirus, Parainfluenza), Bordetella, and Parvo. Proof of vaccination and age must be available upon request. Puppies under four months of age or unaltered dogs will not be permitted entry.

event_name: Carriage Rides at Nay Aug Park's Holiday Light Spectacular
event_description: Join Brookvalley Farm LLC for a horse-drawn carriage ride through the Holiday Light Spectacular at Nay Aug Park in Scranton! The carriage seats four adults comfortably and costs $20 per person and $10 per child ($40 minimum per ride). Children 12 and under must be accompanied by a paying adult. Rides are first-come, first-served. Reservations are not accepted. You can find them in the parking lot on the left, just after entering the light display at the Mulberry Street / Arthur Avenue entrance. Upon arrival, check in with the attendant to be added to the ride list, which can be monitored by visiting www.brookvalleyfarmpa.com. Each ride is approximately 10-15 minutes. Carriage rides are offered from 6 PM to 9 PM. Please note that event dates and times are subject to change. For the most accurate schedule and updates on potential cancellations due to weather or traffic delays, we recommend checking Brookvalley Farm's website. A portion of the proceeds will be donated to the Scranton Municipal Recreation Authority for park improvements, maintenance, and upkeep. NOTE: To avoid traffic blocking emergency entrances to Geisinger Community Medical Center, kindly refrain from using Mulberry Street near the hospital. Instead, please use Arthur Avenue to enter the Mulberry Street entrance for the Nay Aug Park Holiday Light Spectacular.

event_description: Carbondale Holiday Light Parade 🎄 Experience the magic of the season at Carbondale’s Holiday Light Parade on Saturday, December 6, 2025! The City of Carbondale welcomes visitors and locals to this beloved annual tradition, where lighted floats and festive vehicles illuminate the night with stunning holiday displays. Mark your calendar for a night of holiday cheer in Downtown Carbondale!

event_description: Join Black Scranton Project as they kick off Black History Month 2026 with an Opening Reception at the Black Scranton Project Center for Arts & Culture. This is a free event open to everyone. RSVP is encouraged but not required. There is an optional $26 support ticket that includes an exclusive BSP gift. This year’s theme, Black History: Centennial Celebration, honors local Black history during a national moment as the U.S. observes America’s 250th year (America250). The Black Scranton Project is centering the people, stories, and contributions that have shaped Black life in Scranton and Northeastern Pennsylvania. Enjoy a local history exhibition, a gallery talk led by Glynis Johns, Founder & CEO at 3:00 PM, music, light refreshments, and a community gathering.

event_description: Circle Drive-In Flea Fair & Farmers Market Spend your Sunday at the Circle Drive-In Flea Fair & Farmers Market, returning March 15th, 2026, and running every Sunday through November 15th (weather permitting). Held at the Circle Drive-In Theatre, this award-winning outdoor market has been voted The Times-Tribune Readers’ Choice “Best Flea Market” and “Best Drive-In Theatre” for over a decade. Open weekly from 6:00 AM to 2:00 PM, the Giant Flea Fair features hundreds of vendors and draws thousands of shoppers throughout the season. Browse an ever-changing selection of fresh produce, antiques, collectibles, handmade arts and crafts, jewelry, tools, equipment, new and gently used clothing, and so much more. With large 18' x 20' selling spaces, the market offers plenty of room for vendors and a wide variety of finds for visitors. Admission is just $1 per vehicle, making it an affordable and family-friendly way to spend a Sunday morning. Shoppers are encouraged to bring both cash and cards, as payment options vary by vendor. An ATM is conveniently located inside the concession stand. Vendors are welcome to arrive anytime after 5:00 AM to set up. Early-bird pricing is available, and monthly spaces can be reserved by contacting the organizers directly. Please note that weekly vendor payments are made onsite only, and advance reservations for weekly spots are not required. For the latest updates and weather-related announcements, follow the Circle Drive-In Flea Fair on Facebook. Service animals are permitted; however, pets are not allowed on the property. For more on the general flea fair information, rules, and regulations, please visit the Circle Drive-In's website. Plan a scenic drive and discover why the Circle Drive-In Flea Fair & Farmers Market remains a longtime favorite for shopping, fresh finds, and community fun in Lackawanna County.

event_description: 2026 Arts On Fire Festival at the Scranton Iron Furnaces 🔥 The Arts on Fire Festival, presented by the Pennsylvania Anthracite Heritage Museum, returns to the Scranton Iron Furnaces for a FREE, two-day celebration of arts, heritage, industry, and community. Launched in 2009, this annual festival takes place the first weekend of June and brings creative energy to one of Scranton’s most historic sites. On Saturday, June 6th, the festival features hands-on activities, an art and craft market, live musical performances, the ever-popular iron pour, and the Youth Arts Showcase. On Sunday, June 7th, visitors can take part in several workshops and additional activities, making Arts on Fire a weekend-long experience celebrating creativity and community in Scranton, PA. Saturday, June 6, 2026 | 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM Enjoy hands-on activities with the Pennsylvania Anthracite Heritage Museum's partners, live music, craft and artist market, and more! The Iron Pour Visitors can purchase scratch blocks to design custom souvenirs from the festival. Metal artist Brian Glaze will be joined by blacksmiths Cliff Prokop and David Schulte, as well as students from Keystone College, for the ultimate, fiery iron-pouring experience. Visitor scratch blocks will be turned into their very own souvenir iron. Please allow time for the iron pour and cool down. Participants may need to return on a later date to retrieve the finished product. Youth Arts Showcase The local youth will showcase their original art based on the theme, Change . On Saturday, stop by the Youth Arts Showcase tent to check out their work and chat with the young artists about their process and inspiration. Sunday, June 7, 2026 | 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM Come back to the Scranton Iron Furnaces to shop the unique craft and artist market, check out partner activities, and enjoy a workshop or two! Knightsmith Blacksmith Workshops Join expert blacksmith, Chris Knight, for one of two (or both) workshops where you’ll learn blacksmithing basics and get hands-on in the forge and fire. All participants will leave the workshop with their handmade project. This event will run from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM and costs $20-$35 per person. The herb cutter workshops may run past the event’s 4:00 PM end time. NMIH Metal Melting Workshops Science, art, and manufacturing come together in this hands-on, family-friendly workshop. Join National Museum of Industrial History’s historian, Mike Piersa, at the Scranton Iron Furnaces where participants learn how to prepare sand molds to receive molten tin and create a product to take home! This event will take place from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM and costs $30 per person. This workshop is not recommended for children under 8 years old. Anyone under 18 will need to be accompanied by a parent or guardian. Parents and guardians do not have to pay unless taking part in the experience.

event_description: 🫐 Blues, Brews, & BBQ at Lakeland Orchard & Cidery Celebrate summer at Blues, Brews, & BBQ at Lakeland Orchard & Cidery, taking place Thursday, July 2nd through Sunday, July 26th, 2026. Lakeland Orchard’s reimagined Summer Festival brings together fresh blueberries, live bluegrass music, locally brewed beer, and barbecue for a lively seasonal experience. Throughout July, visitors can enjoy pick-your-own blueberries straight from the plant, relax to live bluegrass performances, and explore an expanded barbecue menu featuring slow-smoked favorites and new options. 🫐 Pick Your Own Blueberries Included with admission, guests can pick fresh blueberries directly from the plant. Container size upgrades are available on-site while supplies last, making it easy to bring home extra berries. 🪓 Live Lumberjack Competitions Watch skilled lumberjacks hack, whack, smack, and saw their way through thrilling tests of strength, skill, and creativity during live lumberjack competitions. These high-energy demonstrations are included with admission. 🎸 Live Bluegrass Music in the Cider Garden Enjoy Lakeland Orchard’s largest lineup of bluegrass bands ever, performing fan-favorite covers and original compositions in the Cider Garden. All live music performances are included with admission. 🌸 Plan Your Visit to Lakeland Orchard & Cidery To make the most of your trip, explore our Lakeland Orchard & Cidery page for more information about seasonal festivals, visitor details, and everything you need to plan your experience. Discover upcoming events, learn more about the orchard, and start planning your visit to one of the region’s favorite destinations!

event_description: 🍎 Apple Harvest Festival at Lakeland Orchard & Cidery Celebrate fall at Lakeland Orchard & Cidery’s signature autumn event, the Apple Harvest Festival, taking place Thursday, September 3rd, through Sunday, November 1st, 2026. This beloved festival invites visitors to experience apple picking, family-friendly entertainment, and classic fall treats throughout the orchard. event_name: Austin Burke: NEPA Through and Through
event_description: To say that Austin Burke loves his roots in the anthracite region is an understatement. Burke’s paintings celebrate the richness of life throughout NEPA, where the artist has resided his entire life. After a successful 40-year career as president of the Scranton Chamber of Commerce and working for the state under then-Governor Ed Rendell, Burke returned to his art full time and took further classes at his alma mater, Keystone College, where he was awarded an honorary Doctorate in Human Letters. The exhibition will showcase Burke’s renderings of well-known Scranton and NEPA landmarks. The Everhart is proud to bring Austin Burke’s interpretations to the area, city, and its people he has championed his entire life. There will be an opening reception with the artist in October. 🖼️ Plan Your Visit to the Everhart Museum Planning a visit? Explore our Everhart Museum webpage for current exhibitions, admission information, visitor details, and upcoming events. Find everything you need to make the most of your museum experience.

event_name: 3 Decades Rewind - Iconic Rock Hit from the 60's, 70's & 80's
event_description: Travel back to the golden age of rock: the 60s, 70s, and 80s with 3 Decades Rewind on Friday, October 30th, 2026, at 7:00 PM. 3 Decades Rewind is a powerhouse tribute to the golden age of rock, delivering unforgettable live performances of the most iconic hits from the 60s, 70s, and 80s. With over a decade of shared musical chemistry, the band channels the spirit of the original legends — bringing to life the energy, passion, and authenticity of artists like The Beatles, Paul McCartney, Queen, ELO, The Beach Boys, The Eagles, and Chicago in an outstanding show packed with classic rock hits. Known for packed-to-the-brim shows across the Tri-State area, Florida, and Texas – including a sold-out show at the Westhampton Beach Performing Arts Center in 2025 – 3 Decades Rewind is rapidly expanding its reach nationwide, with a growing list of theater and iconic venue dates coast to coast. Every performance is a celebration of timeless music, performed 100% live and infused with the unique touch of each band member’s individual talent. From soaring harmonies and intricate arrangements to electrifying solos and an explosive horn section that brings the house down, 3 Decades Rewind is more than a cover band – it’s a full-throttle experience that honors the pure, unfiltered energy of rock ‘n’ roll. Tickets are $39-$49 per person plus fees and can be purchased online at The Theater at North's website or in person at the box office on Tuesdays from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM, Wednesdays from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM, Thursdays from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM, and on the day of the show starting at 5:00 PM.

event_description: On Saturday, November 7th, 2026, from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM, the Abington Angels will be returning to host its 13th Annual Marketplace at the Abington Heights Middle School. All proceeds from the Marketplace go directly to the Abington Angels program — the Abington Heights Civic League's charitable program that supports students and their families who are in need. In preparation for Thanksgiving, Winter and Spring breaks, the Abington Angels purchase, package, and distribute the makings for entire holiday meals, as well as pantry staples for each break. Working from “wish lists” created by the children of these families, Abington Angels purchases, wraps, and distributes holiday gifts. The Abington Angels gather and prepare gently used clothing for distribution. The Abington Angels expanded to include school supplies for the elementary schools.

event_description: The NEPA Philharmonic and Music Director Mélisse Brunet return with their second candlelit choral requiem, featuring the transcendental beauty of Brahms’ A German Requiem. In this special candlelit performance of the moving masterpiece in a historic local church, audiences will be immersed in the emotional depth of this humanistic work of mourning, hope, and the beauty of life. Returning for this requiem are audience favorites soprano Jessica Leigh, baritone Sunghoon Han, and the Marywood University Concert Choir. This event will last 70-80 minutes in length with no intermission. Tickets are $29-$53 in advance and $35-$60 at the door for adults, and $16 in advance and $20 at the door for Students (with ID).

event_name: Anthony Nunziata Live in Concert: A Sinatra Christmas
event_description: Back by popular demand, acclaimed classically-trained singer and songwriter Anthony Nunziata brings the romance, swing, and warmth of Frank Sinatra to the holiday season with a festive evening of timeless music. Dubbed “America’s New Romantic Singing Sensation” by BroadwayWorld, Brooklyn-born Nunziata has performed more than 400 concerts worldwide, including a sold-out debut at the legendary Café Carlyle in New York City and appearances with the New York Pops at Carnegie Hall, Detroit Symphony, and Colorado Symphony. Featuring Sinatra favorites like “Fly Me to the Moon,” “The Way You Look Tonight,” "Luck Be a Lady," "The Best is Yet to Come," and “New York, New York,” alongside beloved Christmas & Italian classics including “O Holy Night,” “Ave Maria," "Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” "O Sole Mio," and "Santa Lucia,” A Sinatra Christmas is an elegant, joyful night of great songs, stories of growing up in a crazy Italian family, and plenty of holiday cheer! Special guests during this event include The Valley View High School Choir and Occhipinti Dance Company. Tickets are $40 per person plus fees and can be purchased online at The Theater at North's website or in person at the box office on Tuesdays from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM, Wednesdays from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM, Thursdays from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM, and on the night of the show starting at 5:00 PM.

event_description: Broadway in Scranton presents "A Beautiful Noise" 🎤 Created in collaboration with Neil Diamond himself, A Beautiful Noise is the uplifting true story of how a kid from Brooklyn became a chart-busting, show-stopping American rock icon. With 120 million albums sold, a catalogue of classics like “America,” “Forever in Blue Jeans,” and “Sweet Caroline,” an induction into the Songwriters and Rock and Roll Halls of Fame, a Grammy® Lifetime Achievement Award, and sold-out concerts around the world that made him bigger than Elvis, Neil Diamond’s story was made to shine on Broadway-and head out on the road across America. Like Jersey Boys and Beautiful: The Carole King Musical before it, A Beautiful Noise: The Neil Diamond Musical is an inspiring, exhilarating, energy-filled musical memoir that tells the untold true story of how America’s greatest hitmaker became a star, set to the songs that defined his career. Presented in association with and endorsed by Neil Diamond. The show's runtime is 2 hours and 15 minutes (including intermission) and is recommended for all ages. ⏰ 2027 Show Dates & Times Friday, July 23rd | 7:30 PM Saturday, July 24th | 2:00 PM Saturday, July 24th | 7:30 PM Sunday, July 25th | 1:00 PM 🎭 Explore More of Broadway in Scranton Visit our Broadway in Scranton webpage to explore the 2026–27 season, learn more about upcoming performances, and plan an unforgettable theater experience at the Scranton Cultural Center in Downtown Scranton.
